ctx.x: The only interesting thing musically that happened for me on during the next few weeks was a concert/the 9th of June at the Town Hall. This concert was presented by my old friend Timmie Rosenkrantz, and the line up was another who's who inthe jazz world. Red Norvo had an orchestra composed of Joe (Flip) Phillips, Shorty Rodgers, Aaron Sachs, Eddie Bert, Remo Palmieri, Teddy Wilson and Slam Stewart. A fellow named Fran Warren did a voice and drum solo. Don Byas and Slam Stewart did a couple of duets. Erroll Garner…

In July, I was engaged by George Johnson to play one month in the Savoy in Boston. A nice blowing little fellow named Johnny Hartsfield was the tenor man and Red Richards was the pianist. Both of them had been in New York for quite some time, but it was the first time I had met them. Johnny was a nice guy until he had taken a few drinks, and then he was a little devil. We all sat down to play except George, and the bass player, who was a fellow from Boston. One night, Johnny had had a few tastes and he would…

I had been to Boston a few times before. Once for a week with Ralph Cooper, another time ona jam session at the Ken Club with Hawk and once with Benny Carter in 1941, and also Andy Kirk, but it was not a city that amused me. About one week after we were there I decided to have a tooth next to the middle one on the right side taken out, and a new one put in, because this one had rotted away until it was only half a tooth.
